prompt: Where should the validation tier be authoritative? The design proposes a `validation_tier` column authored by the coordinator at filing time, with the PR body naming evidence against it.
choices: Work-item column, authored at filing time (as designed)
PR-body section only, enforced by the review lane
Both, with the column authoritative and the PR body required to match
Both, with the PR body allowed to override the filed tier when the worker justifies it

prompt: Should tier `unit`/`automated` evidence require naming specific Bazel targets that are then mechanically resolved against the PR's bazel-testlogs artifacts? This is the strongest anti-self-report mechanism but adds friction to every PR.

Should the `scripted` fake agent driver be registered in the production DriverRegistry, or gated so it only exists in test builds? Registering it means the production spawn path is genuinely what runs in tests, but it also means a fake driver slug is visible in shipped binaries.
choices: Register it unconditionally — production path fidelity matters more
Register it only under a testonly cfg / feature flag
Register it unconditionally but hide it from user-facing driver listings

prompt: Should `DispatchEvent` become a stability-committed interface (additive-only evolution, wire goldens, compat obligations)? It is already read by bossctl and the macOS app, so this mostly formalises reality — but it does constrain future changes.

Flakiness budget: the design proposes at most 5 quarantined targets repo-wide and a 14-day maximum quarantine age before it escalates to a blocking attention item. Are those the right numbers, and who owns the escalation?
